findings.claim: The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (lines 29-34, used at line 58) hand-duplicates the zod schema and flattens the discriminated union. As a result, `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` with no teamId now compiles. At runtime it fails safeParse, options becomes null, and every query silently returns 1=0 (an empty result).
findings.evidence: Diff hunk `-    options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions;` / `+    options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions;`. Line 36 already derives the correct type from the schema at lines 10-27. git grep finds no production callers, so nothing is affected today. open-code-review confirms the runtime path fails closed (1=0), which matches the claim; it is not a leak. Reasoned; no seat ran tsc.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Minor, because it fails closed and has no callers. Fix: delete lines 29-34 and type the constructor with the zod-inferred InsightsBookingServiceOptions, as on the base. That restores the compile-time error and removes the hand-kept duplicate.

verifier.reason: The patch changes the constructor parameter (insightsBooking.ts:58) to the hand-written flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (lines 29-34). That type has `teamId?: number` for every scope, so `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` with no teamId type-checks. The zod discriminated union (lines 10-27) still requires teamId for team scope, so safeParse fails at line 62 and options becomes null. Every query then gets `NOTHING_CONDITION` (1=0), which is an empty result and never a leak (lines 126-127, 72-73).

findings.claim: The public condition getters return OR fragments without outer parentheses. Affected: org/team auth at 171-174 and 204-207; the eventTypeId-only filter at 106; getBaseConditions with no filters returns auth bare at 75. A caller writing `WHERE ${base} AND x` gets `A OR (B AND x)`, so team-branch rows skip the caller's date or status predicate. Results stay within the authorized set but counts are inflated.
findings.evidence: Both seats found that the reduce builds `(A) OR (B)` with no outer brackets and that line 75 returns authConditions unwrapped. findMany, the old composition point, is removed, so callers must now compose raw SQL. The old Prisma `AND: [...]` composed safely, so this is a regression in the contract. The only DB test (~438-481) runs `WHERE ${base}` alone, in user scope or with filters (parens added at 73), so it cannot catch this. Proposed red test (superpowers): org scope, no filters, a team booking outside a date range, `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" > now()`; that booking is returned. Reasoned; not run.
findings.reason: Raised by only two seats, so it goes in the appendix and is not fixed, per the merge rule. Severity stays Important; unverified. The red test above would settle it. Note: both correctness seats raised it independently with the same mechanism, and no seat report disputes it. It is the strongest unaddressed correctness claim in this review.

These come from findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no orderBy, and Prisma.Sql equality includes the order of the values array. The problem pre-exists: the old object-based assertion had the same order dependence. Reasoned.
